sequence_description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt unsigned request object (alg=none) to override semantic auth parameters (redirect_uri/scope) and compare to a normal auth request. Secure behavior is explicit rejection or ignoring the unsigned request object.
description: [LLM-Judge] Attack attempt returned HTTP 404 (Not Found) rather than an explicit OIDC error response, which may indicate misrouting or an endpoint exposure/configuration issue that prevents proper request-object validation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Attack attempt returned HTTP 404 (Not Found) rather than an explicit OIDC error response, which may indicate misrouting or an endpoint exposure/configuration issue that prevents proper request-object validation.

sequence_description: Brokered-flow attack: token exchange with a subject_token that is syntactically a JWT but signed with an untrusted key (resign_attacker_key). Secure behavior is rejection; include a control exchange using a known-good subject_token from password login to ensure the grant path works.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange accepted a JWT subject_token signed with an untrusted key, resulting in a valid session and granted identity (signature validation / key trust bypass).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange accepted a JWT subject_token signed with an untrusted key, resulting in a valid session and granted identity (signature validation / key trust bypass).

sequence_description: Attempt to escalate scopes/claims via RFC8693 token exchange: obtain a limited-scope token, then exchange it while requesting expanded scopes (groups/profile/federated:id).
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange succeeded and returned expanded identity attributes (groups/policies/display_name) even though the initial limited-scope authorization never produced a valid token (invalid_grant), making the scope-escalation test inconclusive and suggesting possible improper token-exchange authorization checks.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange succeeded and returned expanded identity attributes (groups/policies/display_name) even though the initial limited-scope authorization never produced a valid token (invalid_grant), making the scope-escalation test inconclusive and suggesting possible improper token-exchange authorization checks.

sequence_description: Token exchange: present a subject_token minted via one upstream OIDC connector but claim it belongs to a different connector_id (issuer mismatch). Dex should reject to prevent cross-connector authorization confusion.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange accepted a subject_token while claiming a different connector_id (issuer/connector mismatch), enabling cross-connector authorization confusion.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange accepted a subject_token while claiming a different connector_id (issuer/connector mismatch), enabling cross-connector authorization confusion.
